title: Withheld Cause / Only the Consequence Is Shown

source_refs.author: Classical narrative-film practice
source_refs.title: Ellipsis and offscreen action
source_refs.cultural_context: Continuity editing in which a cut skips the act and keeps the aftermath readable

observed_structure: A stable situation is established so the audience knows who is present and what the place allows.
The next view presents the aftermath, and the act that produced it is not depicted.
What remains is enough to name the consequence, and still not enough to see the cause.
dramatic_operations: show only the consequence while the cause stays withheld
occupied presence becomes an emptied room
cinematic_affordances: cut from the last stable moment straight to the aftermath
the triggering act kept outside the frame
one remaining object whose new position is the evidence
audio of the event continuing without a picture of the act
cultural_scope: general film ellipsis; the withheld event must stay inferable from project evidence
misuse_risks: hiding the cause because the action was never decided
a gap that removes information the next choice depends on
using every skipped beat as mystery branding

variables: who can still read the remainder
next action taken with the remainder

transferable_structure: an emptied room shows only the consequence while the cause stays withheld and the removal is never shown
non_transferable_surface: a specific film's missing assault, signature insert, or copied gap between two famous shots
